tool_input.content:
On aurora-lab (kind cluster, cluster_id kubeconfig-ca6bd1b97359856d), namespace `shop`, Deployment `worker` revision 2 had a new pod stuck Pending with event:
`FailedScheduling: 0/3 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had untolerated taint(s), 2 Insufficient cpu.`

**Root cause:** container resources.requests.cpu was set to `"64"` (64 whole CPU cores) instead of a millicore value like `"50m"`/`"64m"`. Every node in the cluster only has 10 allocatable CPUs, so this can never schedule. Confirmed via comparing to the sibling (previous revision) pod which correctly requests `cpu: 50m, memory: 64Mi`.

**Diagnostic signature:** `kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration` annotation on the Deployment showed the OLD correct value (`cpu: "50m"`) while the live `spec.template.spec.containers[].resources` showed the bad value (`cpu: "64"`) — strong evidence of an out-of-band `kubectl edit`/`set resources`/`patch` rather than a GitOps/`kubectl apply` change. Check this annotation-vs-live-spec mismatch whenever a Deployment's "revision" bumped shortly before a scheduling failure.

**How to apply:** For any `KubePodNotReady`/`FailedScheduling` alert, first run `kubectl describe pod <pending-pod>` to get the exact FailedScheduling reason, then compare the pod's resource requests against sibling pods of the same app from the previous (still-Running) ReplicaSet. A request value that's 100-1000x larger than siblings, or missing the `m` suffix, points to a typo/manual-edit resource misconfiguration rather than real capacity growth.

**Fix:** `kubectl set resources deployment/<name> -n <ns> -c <container> --requests=cpu=<correct_value>` to match the known-good sibling, or `kubectl rollout undo deployment/<name> -n <ns>` if a healthy previous revision/ReplicaSet still exists.
